suppliers.name: Pirelli
suppliers.summary:
Formula One cars run on specialised racing tyres supplied exclusively by Pirelli, an Italian manufacturer. The company has been the sole supplier since 2011, when it won a three-year contract; the deal is currently set to last through the 2027 season.

Each weekend Pirelli nominates three dry compounds from its C1 (hardest) to C5 (softest), naming them hard, medium and soft with white, yellow and red sidewalls respectively. Two treaded wet-weather tyres are supplied at every Grand Prix too, green for intermediate and blue for full wet. Drivers must use at least two dry compounds during a race.

suppliers.name: Michelin
suppliers.summary:
Michelin has been MotoGP's official tyre supplier since 2016, returning after Bridgestone withdrew at the end of 2015. It had previously left the series at the end of 2008 when it did not enter a bid for the single-provider rule introduced in 2009.

On race day, viewers see riders choose compounds based on bike feel during practice and warm-up laps plus predicted weather. Softer compounds give more grip but wear faster; harder ones last longer. If rain falls, riders pit to swap to fully treaded wet tyres under the flag-to-flag rule.

suppliers.name: Goodyear
suppliers.summary:
Goodyear supplies the tyres for NASCAR stock car racing, having done so since 1954. It has been the sole supplier since 1975 apart from short intervals, and in 1997 became the exclusive tyre provider for the three national series, which include the Cup Series.

On race day, viewers may notice how rubber compounds are used in tyre construction and how stagger - tyres of different circumference at different positions - affects handling. These settings are set by NASCAR and Goodyear engineers and cannot be adjusted by individual teams. Changing weather can also influence a car's handling, and rain forces oval races to stop immediately.

photo.caption: Goodyear Eagle tyres in the pit lane

suppliers.name: Firestone
suppliers.summary:
Firestone supplies the tyres for IndyCar, having provided them from the 1996 season before becoming the sole supplier in 2000. Goodyear had supplied several teams between 1996 and 1999 before withdrawing their support, and Firestone will remain the only tyre maker until the 2030 season.

On race day the compounds differ by mounting position, with unique primary and alternative specifications for dry road and street events alongside specially designed full-rain tyres. There are no intermediate rain tyres, so only dry or all-rain options are available.
